top_temples.name: Barpeta Satra (Kirtan Ghar)
top_temples.location_note: Central Barpeta town; founded 1583 AD by Madhavdeva, houses the largest Kirtan Ghar (prayer hall) in Assam, a major Neo-Vaishnavite pilgrimage center.

top_temples.name: Sundaridiya Satra
top_temples.location_note: Near Barpeta town; established by Madhavdeva after leaving Ganakkuchi Satra, a distinct historic satra from the main Kirtan Ghar.

top_temples.name: Raidongia Dol (Shiva Dol)
top_temples.location_note: Near Dihingia Barbarua road, Dibrugarh; a 45-ft tall temple with multiple Shiva lingas.

top_temples.name: Sri Jagannath Temple (Shrikshetra Dhaam)
top_temples.location_note: Dibrugarh; built in 2014 as a replica of the Jagannath Temple in Puri, Odisha.

top_temples.name: Radha Krishna Mandir (Jalan Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: Dibrugarh town; one of the well-known Krishna temples of Upper Assam.

top_temples.name: Durga Temple, Dibrugarh
top_temples.location_note: Dibrugarh; especially lively during Durga Puja celebrations.

top_temples.name: Dehing Satra
top_temples.location_note: Near Dibrugarh; a 17th-century Vaishnavite satra with traditional Assamese architecture.

top_temples.name: Kamakhya Temple
top_temples.location_note: Nilachal Hill, part of the greater Guwahati/Dispur metro area; one of the four major Shakti Peethas in India.

top_temples.name: Umananda Temple
top_temples.location_note: Peacock Island on the Brahmaputra, within the Guwahati/Dispur metro area; built by Ahom King Gadadhar Singha (1681-1696), on the world's smallest inhabited river island.

top_temples.name: Ugratara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Uzan Bazaar, eastern Guwahati/Dispur area; built by Ahom king Shiv Singh in 1725, an important Shakti shrine distinct from Kamakhya.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple, Guwahati
top_temples.location_note: Ulubari Chariali, near Dispur; white marble-floored temple on a hillock.

top_temples.name: Doul Govinda Temple
top_temples.location_note: North Guwahati, at the foothills of Chandrabharati Hill; over 150 years old, renowned for its five-day Holi celebrations.

top_temples.name: Kamakhya Temple
top_temples.location_note: Nilachal Hill, Guwahati; one of the four major Shakti Peethas in India, Guwahati's defining shrine.

top_temples.name: Umananda Temple
top_temples.location_note: Peacock Island on the Brahmaputra, Guwahati; built by Ahom King Gadadhar Singha (1681-1696), on the world's smallest inhabited river island.

top_temples.name: Navagraha Temple
top_temples.location_note: Chitrachal Hill, Guwahati; an important astrological and astronomical site historically.

top_temples.name: Sukreswar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Sukreswar Hill on the Brahmaputra bank, Guwahati; dates to the era of Ahom king Prithu Singha, a major Shaivite site.

top_temples.name: Basistha Temple (Vashistha Ashram)
top_temples.deity: Shiva, associated with sage Vashistha's ashram
top_temples.location_note: At the confluence of the Sandhya, Kanta, and Lalita rivulets, Guwahati; a scenic hillside shrine distinct from the Kamakhya/Umananda temples.

top_temples.name: Hayagriva Madhava Temple
top_temples.location_note: Manikuta Hill, Hajo; one of Assam's most important Vaishnava tirthas, held sacred by both Hindus and Buddhists, dating from the 6th century.

top_temples.name: Kedareswar Temple (Kedar Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Atop Kedar Hill in Hajo, a stone-built shrine distinct from Hayagriva Madhava, reached via a hilly footpath.

top_temples.name: Dhekiakhowa Bornamghar
top_temples.location_note: Jorhat district; established by saint Madhavdeva, notable for a continuously burning lamp for roughly 500 years, recorded in the India Book of Records.

top_temples.name: Burigosain Devalay (Buri Gossain Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Heart of Jorhat city; built in the 18th century by Ahom King Rajeshwar Singha.

top_temples.name: Bilvesvar Shiva Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 35 km from Jorhat town on NH 37; features a holy tank built by Ruchinath Buragohain.

top_temples.name: Hatibaruah Namghar
top_temples.location_note: Jorhat district; a traditional Assamese prayer hall.

top_temples.name: Auniati Satra
top_temples.location_note: Majuli, near Jorhat; founded by Niranjan Pathakdeva, renowned for its Paalnaam ritual and Apsara dance tradition.

top_temples.name: Madan Kamdev Temple (Kameswar Shiva Shrine)
top_temples.deity: Shiva, linked to the Kamadeva revival legend
top_temples.location_note: Baihata Chariali, about 40 km from Guwahati; the principal reconstructed shrine among 10th-12th century Pala-era ruins, nicknamed the 'Khajuraho of Assam'.

top_temples.name: Devi Shrine, Madan Kamdev Ruins
top_temples.deity: Devi (Shakti form, linked to the Kamakhya legend tied to the site's name)
top_temples.location_note: A subsidiary shrine among the excavated ruins of more than 20 temples at the same Madan Kamdev archaeological complex.

top_temples.name: Maha Mrityunjay Temple
top_temples.location_note: Nagaon; houses what is claimed to be the world's largest Shivalinga.

top_temples.name: Gatanga Temple
top_temples.location_note: Nagaon district; known for its week-long Naam Kirtan Festival held each March.

top_temples.name: Nag Shankar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Nagaon; believed to be one of the oldest temples in the state.

top_temples.name: Silghat Trishuldhari Temple
top_temples.location_note: Silghat, Nagaon district, on the Brahmaputra.

top_temples.name: Hatimura Temple
top_temples.location_note: Silghat, Nagaon district; a Shakti temple with the goddess depicted slaying the buffalo demon.

top_temples.name: Bhuban Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: Atop Bhuban Hill, about 50 km from Silchar in Cachar district; South Assam's most famous Shiva shrine, major hub during Maha Shivaratri and the annual Bhuvan Mela.

top_temples.name: Kanch Kanti Kali Mandir
top_temples.location_note: About 14 km from Silchar city centre; established by the Kachari dynasty, one of the most revered temples in South Assam, dating to the 19th century.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple, Silchar
top_temples.location_note: Ambikapatty area, Silchar; built and maintained by the International Society for Krishna Consciousness.

top_temples.name: Salganga Vishnu Temple
top_temples.location_note: Salganga village, about 22 km from Silchar on the way to Kumbhirgram airport.

top_temples.name: Ramakrishna Mission Sevashrama (Universal Temple of Sri Ramakrishna)
top_temples.location_note: Silchar; the mission was founded in 1924, and its newly built temple was consecrated in March 2025 for its centenary.

top_temples.name: Shiva Dol (Sivadol)
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Sivasagar (Borpukhuri) tank; built in 1734 by Bar Raja Ambika, queen of Ahom king Swargadeo Siva Singha, at 104 ft the tallest Shiva temple in Northeast India.

top_temples.name: Vishnu Dol
top_temples.location_note: Part of the same Sivasagar tank temple complex as Shiva Dol, built in the same era (1734), a distinct smaller shrine alongside Devi Dol.

top_temples.name: Mahabhairab Temple
top_temples.location_note: North of Tezpur town, Sonitpur district; believed established by King Bana, houses one of the world's largest Shiva lingams.

top_temples.name: Bamuni Hills Ruins
top_temples.location_note: Tezpur, Sonitpur district; 9th-10th century ASI-protected ruins believed to have had a central Vishnu shrine with four Shiva shrines at the corners.

top_temples.name: Tilinga Mandir (Bell Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Bordubi, about 7 km from Tinsukia; holds the Limca Book of Records title for the largest collection of bells, offered by devotees.

top_temples.name: Shiv Dham
top_temples.location_note: AT Road, Tinsukia town centre; unique for its Shiva statue seated at the centre of a water kund.

top_temples.name: Nepali Mandir (Nepali Durga Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: Sripuria Pathar, Tinsukia; centre of the town's Nepali community Durga Puja celebrations.

top_temples.name: Panchmukhi Hanuman Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Ambika Rai Choudhary Path, Hijuguri, Tinsukia.

top_temples.name: Radha Krishna Mandir
top_temples.location_note: AT Road, Tinsukia town.
